title: Realizing a prescribed monoidal incidence diagram by an inert relative limit cone
statement: Use the universe, nerve and coherent diagram conventions of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], monoidal infinity categories and inert maps of [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category], cocartesian edges of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], and joins and relative limits of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone]. Let $p:\mathcal V^\otimes\to N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$ be a monoidal infinity category and $r\geq0$. Let $I_r$ be the finite category with objects $e_1,\ldots,e_r,v_0,\ldots,v_r$, nonidentity arrows $e_j\to v_{j-1},v_j$, and no others. Define $b_r:N(I_r)\to N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$ by $b_r(e_j)=[1]$, $b_r(v_i)=[0]$, with the two endpoint maps on the displayed arrows. Let $\bar b_r:\Delta^0\star N(I_r)\to N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$ have apex $[r]$; its legs are opposite to the inclusions of the consecutive edges and vertices into $[r]$. For every coherent diagram $f:N(I_r)\to\mathcal V^\otimes$ with $pf=b_r$ exactly, there exists $\bar f:\Delta^0\star N(I_r)\to\mathcal V^\otimes$ such that $\bar f|_{N(I_r)}=f$ and $p\bar f=\bar b_r$ exactly. Every apex leg is $p$-cocartesian, and $\bar f$ is a relative $p$-limit diagram. In particular, the endpoints, both arrows to a shared endpoint, and all their incidence triangles are retained with their specified restrictions. For $r=0$ one can take the apex to be $f(v_0)$ and its sole leg to be the identity. No colimit hypothesis is imposed on $\mathcal V$.

proof.text: For $r=0$, $I_0$ is the one-object category on $v_0$. Use the identity edge of $f(v_0)$ as the cone, over the identity of $[0]$. In the dual constant-source test of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-constant-test], restriction of this cone gives identity maps on both the total and base mapping spaces, so its square is a homotopy pullback. It is therefore a $p$-limit. Its edge is $p$-cocartesian by the degenerate-edge clause of [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality]. This has exactly the required boundary and base. Henceforth suppose $r>0$.

source.place: Definition 3.1.13(2)-(3), Appendix A.3.1(2) and A.3.4; agent expansion of the prescribed-boundary incidence cone, using the existing relative right Kan cone comparison.

proof.text: Write $E=\mathcal V^\otimes$ and $B=N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$. The map $p:E\to B$ is an inner fibration by [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category] and [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Every equivalence in $B$ is an identity, since an order isomorphism of finite ordinals is the identity. Each has the identity equivalence as a lift at any prescribed source. Thus $p$ is an isofibration in the explicit sense of [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation]. All indexing categories used below are finite nerves and fit the stipulated universe.

source.place: Definition 3.1.13(2)-(3), Appendix A.3.1(2) and A.3.4; agent expansion of the prescribed-boundary incidence cone, using the existing relative right Kan cone comparison.

proof.text: If $z\in E_{[0]}$, the arity-zero mapping axiom in [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category] gives $\operatorname{Map}^{\psi}_E(D,z)\simeq *$ for every $D$ and every $\psi:pD\to[0]$. Since the base mapping space is discrete, this says $\operatorname{Map}_E(D,z)\to\operatorname{Map}_B(pD,[0])$ is an equivalence: it is the disjoint union of its contractible homotopy fibers. The dual constant-source criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-constant-test] now says the empty cone with apex $z$ is a $p$-limit over the empty base diagram with apex $[0]$. This is relative finality over $[0]$, with no terminal object assumed in $\mathcal V$.

source.place: Definition 3.1.13(2)-(3), Appendix A.3.1(2) and A.3.4; agent expansion of the prescribed-boundary incidence cone, using the existing relative right Kan cone comparison.

proof.text: Let $A\subseteq C=N(I_r)$ be the full discrete subcategory on $e_1,\ldots,e_r$. For $e_j$, the outgoing category $A\times_C C_{e_j/}$ of [lem-coef-relative-right-kan-universal-restriction] is the singleton identity arrow; its cone under $f$ is the identity cone, a $p$-limit by the constant-source criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-constant-test]. For $v_i$ this outgoing category is empty, since no arrow starts at $v_i$ and ends at an $e_j$. Its $f$-cone has apex $f(v_i)\in E_{[0]}$ and is a $p$-limit by Step 3. Thus the given functor $f$, including its prescribed endpoint arrows, is a pointwise $p$-right Kan extension of $f|_A$ over $b_r$, with exactly the outgoing categories required by the cone-comparison lemma.

source.place: Definition 3.1.13(2)-(3), Appendix A.3.1(2) and A.3.4; agent expansion of the prescribed-boundary incidence cone, using the existing relative right Kan cone comparison.

proof.text: Put $x_j=f(e_j)$. The fiber Segal equivalence $E_{[r]}\simeq E_{[1]}^r$ of [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category] is essentially surjective. Choose $c\in E_{[r]}$, cocartesian projections $c\to y_j$ over $\rho_j$, and fiber equivalences $y_j\to x_j$ representing that essential surjectivity. An equivalence over an identity is $p$-cocartesian by [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion]: its two horizontal precomposition maps are equivalences, hence the square is a homotopy pullback. Fill an inner $2$-horn to compose each projection with $y_j\to x_j$, over $\rho_j$, using [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. By [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality] the resulting edges $a_j:c\to x_j$ are cocartesian. Because $A$ is discrete, these edges alone define a map $q_A:\Delta^0\star A\to E$ over $\bar b_r|_{\Delta^0\star A}$ whose boundary is exactly $f|_A$. No simultaneous realization of the endpoints has yet been assumed.

source.place: Definition 3.1.13(2)-(3), Appendix A.3.1(2) and A.3.4; agent expansion of the prescribed-boundary incidence cone, using the existing relative right Kan cone comparison.

proof.text: The cone $q_A$ is a $p$-limit. Indeed, the upper-right space in the dual constant-source test of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-constant-test] is $\prod_j\operatorname{Map}_E(D,x_j)$ because $A$ is discrete. The lower row is the corresponding product restriction of base mapping spaces. Its homotopy-pullback comparison, over any fixed $\phi:pD\to[r]$, is exactly $\operatorname{Map}^{\phi}_E(D,c)\to\prod_j\operatorname{Map}^{\rho_j\phi}_E(D,x_j)$. This is an equivalence by the relative product axiom of [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category], which applies to every choice of cocartesian projection edges, in particular the exact-target edges $a_j$ of Step 5. All base mapping spaces are discrete, so these fiber equivalences give the required homotopy pullback square.

source.place: Definition 3.1.13(2)-(3), Appendix A.3.1(2) and A.3.4; agent expansion of the prescribed-boundary incidence cone, using the existing relative right Kan cone comparison.

proof.text: Apply the cone-comparison clause of [lem-coef-relative-right-kan-universal-restriction] with $C=N(I_r)$, its full subcategory $A$, $H=f$, the isofibration $p$ of Step 2, and base cone $b=\bar b_r$. Step 4 verified its pointwise right Kan hypothesis; Steps 5-6 provide the exact cone $q_A$ and its $p$-limit property. The lemma produces $\bar f:\Delta^0\star N(I_r)\to E$ with $\bar f|_C=f$, $\bar f|_{\Delta^0\star A}=q_A$, and $p\bar f=\bar b_r$, all exactly. It also says this cone is a $p$-limit. In particular its apex is the already chosen $c$ and its edge legs are the $a_j$. The original two arrows to each shared endpoint are fixed as part of $f$; the incidence triangles and all simplicial restrictions are supplied by this exact cone extension, rather than by choosing unrelated homotopies.

source.place: Definition 3.1.13(2)-(3), Appendix A.3.1(2) and A.3.4; agent expansion of the prescribed-boundary incidence cone, using the existing relative right Kan cone comparison.

proof.text:
For each vertex leg $h_i:c	o z_i=f(v_i)$ of $ ar f$, let $
u_i:[r]	o[0]$ be its base and choose a $p$-cocartesian lift $u_i:c	o z'_i$ over $
u_i$, using [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. The initiality clause of [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality] in $L(c,
u_i)$ supplies a comparison $k_i:z'_i	o z_i$ over $1_{[0]}$ and a coherent triangle $k_i u_i\simeq h_i$ with the specified base. The Segal equivalence $E_{[0]}\simeq *$ of [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category] makes every edge of this fiber an equivalence, so $k_i$ is an equivalence. Its mapping square is a homotopy pullback by [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion], as for equivalences in Step 5. Cocartesian composition in the same initiality lemma therefore makes $h_i$ cocartesian. Together with the $a_j$ this proves cocartesianness of every apex leg. Only finite tuple realization and the empty relative limit over $[0]$ were used; no colimits in $\mathcal V$ were required.

source.place: Definition 3.1.13(2)-(3), Appendix A.3.1(2) and A.3.4; agent expansion of the prescribed-boundary incidence cone, using the existing relative right Kan cone comparison.

lean.statement: theorem operadic_typec_incidence_cone {E : SSet.{u}} [Quasicategory E] (p : E ⟶ monoidalSimplexBase.{u}) (hp : IsMonoidalInfinityCategory p) (r : ℕ) (d : TypeCIncidenceData r) (f : CategoryTheory.nerve d.I ⟶ E) (hf : f ≫ p = d.b) : ∃ barf : leftJoinCone (CategoryTheory.nerve d.I) ⟶ E, leftJoinConeInclusion (CategoryTheory.nerve d.I) ≫ barf = f ∧ barf ≫ p = d.barB ∧ IsRelativeLimitDiagram p barf ∧ (∀ x : (CategoryTheory.nerve d.I) _⦋0⦌, IsCocartesianEdge p (typeCIncidenceConeEdge x ≫ barf)) ∧ (r = 0 → ∃ x : (CategoryTheory.nerve d.I) _⦋0⦌, orderedJoinInl (Δ[0] : SSet.{u}) (CategoryTheory.nerve d.I) ≫ barf = SSet.yonedaEquiv.symm (f.app _ x) ∧ typeCIncidenceConeEdge x ≫ barf = SSet.yonedaEquiv.symm (E.map (SimplexCategory.σ 0).op (f.app _ x)))
